passages.title: 납품 지연에 대한 해명과 보상 제안
passages.passage:
From: Elena Vargas, Account Manager, Meridian Components
To: Jonas Feld, Procurement Director, Atlas Manufacturing
Subject: Delayed shipment of order #AT-2287

Dear Mr. Feld,

I am writing regarding your order of hydraulic valves, which was scheduled to arrive at your Dortmund plant on March 3. Due to an equipment malfunction at our Rotterdam facility, production fell behind by approximately one week, and we now expect the shipment to reach you no later than March 11.

We recognize that this delay may disrupt your assembly schedule. To mitigate the inconvenience, we are prepared to cover the cost of expedited freight and to apply a 12 percent discount to this invoice. In addition, our engineering team can arrange a video call this week to help your staff adjust the installation timeline.

We value our four-year partnership with Atlas Manufacturing and are taking steps to ensure that a single point of failure cannot halt production again. A second production line will be operational by June.

Sincerely,
Elena Vargas

questions.q: Why did Ms. Vargas write the email?
choices: To explain a delay and offer compensation
To request an extension on a payment
To announce a new product line
To terminate a supply contract
questions.exKo: 지연 사유(장비 고장) 설명과 함께 특급 운송비 부담, 12% 할인 등 보상안을 제시하는 것이 메일의 목적입니다.

questions.q: What is suggested about Meridian Components?
choices: It currently relies on a single production line
It has never missed a delivery before
It plans to close its Rotterdam facility
It manufactures its products in Dortmund
questions.exKo: a single point of failure cannot halt production again과 6월에 두 번째 생산 라인이 가동된다는 내용에서, 현재는 생산 라인이 하나뿐임을 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word "mitigate" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
choices: lessen
measure
multiply
monitor
questions.exKo: mitigate는 '완화하다, 줄이다'라는 뜻이므로 lessen이 가장 가깝습니다.

passages.title: 재택근무 정책을 둘러싼 기업들의 실험 기사
passages.passage:
THE COMMERCE JOURNAL

When Halbrook Insurance announced that its 2,000 employees could work from anywhere permanently, industry observers predicted a wave of similar policies. Eighteen months later, the picture is considerably more nuanced.

A survey of 140 mid-sized firms conducted by the Radley Institute found that while 78 percent now permit some form of remote work, only 9 percent have adopted fully location-independent policies. The majority have settled on hybrid arrangements, typically requiring two or three days in the office each week.

"Companies discovered that collaboration did not suffer as much as they feared, but spontaneous mentoring did," said Dr. Priya Raman, the study's lead author. Junior employees at fully remote firms reported 40 percent fewer informal learning interactions than their hybrid counterparts.

Notably, firms that tied office attendance to specific activities - such as project kickoffs or client workshops - reported higher employee satisfaction than those that mandated fixed weekly days, suggesting that the reason for commuting matters as much as the frequency.

questions.q: What is the main point of the article?
choices: Most firms have chosen hybrid work over fully remote policies
Remote work has been abandoned by most companies
Halbrook Insurance has canceled its remote work policy
Office attendance no longer affects employee satisfaction
questions.exKo: 전면 원격근무를 도입한 기업은 9%에 불과하고 대다수가 하이브리드 방식에 정착했다는 것이 기사의 핵심입니다.

questions.q: According to Dr. Raman, what suffered most at fully remote firms?
choices: Informal mentoring of junior employees
Client communication
Project deadlines
Data security
questions.exKo: spontaneous mentoring did (suffer)와 신입 직원들의 비공식 학습 교류가 40% 적었다는 부분에서 확인할 수 있습니다.

questions.q: What can be inferred about firms with activity-based attendance policies?
choices: Employees respond better when office visits have a clear purpose
They require more office days than other firms
They pay higher salaries than fully remote firms
They were excluded from the Radley Institute survey
questions.exKo: 목적이 있는 출근을 요구한 기업의 만족도가 더 높았다는 마지막 문단에서, 출근의 '이유'가 중요함을 추론할 수 있습니다.

passages.title: 계약 협상 전략 논의 채팅
passages.passage:
Owen Brandt (16:41): Rika, quick update. Coleman's team just countered - they want the maintenance clause extended to five years at the current rate.
Rika Tanaka (16:42): Five years without a price adjustment? Our costs rise every year. That would erode the entire margin by year three.
Owen Brandt (16:43): Agreed. But they hinted they would sign this week if we accept.
Rika Tanaka (16:45): Tempting, but let's not give it away. Offer three years fixed, then annual adjustments capped at 4 percent. We keep the margin, they get predictability.
Owen Brandt (16:46): And if they push back?
Rika Tanaka (16:47): Then we trade it for the exclusivity clause they keep resisting. One concession deserves another.
Owen Brandt (16:48): Understood. Drafting the counteroffer now.

questions.q: At 16:45, what does Ms. Tanaka mean when she writes, "let's not give it away"?
choices: They should not accept unfavorable terms just to close quickly
They should keep the negotiation confidential
They should cancel the maintenance clause entirely
They should offer the service for free
questions.exKo: 이번 주 서명 가능성이 유혹적이지만(Tempting) 마진을 지키는 역제안을 하자는 흐름에서, 서두르느라 불리한 조건을 내주지 말자는 의미임을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.q: What will Mr. Brandt most likely do next?
choices: Prepare a revised proposal for Coleman's team
Sign the five-year maintenance clause
Schedule a meeting with the legal team
Withdraw from the negotiation
questions.exKo: 마지막 메시지 Drafting the counteroffer now에서 역제안서를 작성할 것임을 알 수 있습니다.

questions.q: What does Ms. Tanaka suggest doing if the counteroffer is rejected?
choices: Exchanging the concession for the exclusivity clause
Lowering the annual price cap
Extending the contract to ten years
Asking for an immediate payment
questions.exKo: we trade it for the exclusivity clause에서 상대가 거부해 온 독점 조항과 맞바꾸자고 제안하고 있습니다.

passages.title: 전사 경비 처리 시스템 전환 공지
passages.passage:
MEMO: TRANSITION TO THE APEX EXPENSE PLATFORM

To: All Department Heads
From: Finance Operations

Beginning August 1, all employee expense claims must be submitted through the Apex platform. The legacy paper-based process will be retired in stages, as outlined below.

Phase 1 (July 1-31): Both systems accepted. Employees are strongly encouraged to file at least one claim in Apex to become familiar with the interface.
Phase 2 (August 1-September 30): Apex only. Paper forms will be returned unprocessed. Receipts must be photographed and uploaded within 30 days of the transaction date.
Phase 3 (October 1): Claims older than 60 days will require written justification and director-level approval.

Reimbursements filed through Apex are processed within five business days - roughly half the current turnaround. Department heads should ensure that every team member completes the 20-minute online tutorial by July 25. Completion rates will be reported to the executive committee.

Questions may be directed to expensehelp@apex-support.com.

questions.q: What happens to paper forms submitted in September?
choices: They will be returned without processing
They will be processed with a delay
They will require director approval
They will be forwarded to Apex support
questions.exKo: Phase 2(8월 1일~9월 30일)에는 Apex만 허용되며 Paper forms will be returned unprocessed라고 명시되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What is implied about the current reimbursement process?
choices: It takes about ten business days
It requires director-level approval
It is handled by an outside vendor
It accepts photographed receipts
questions.exKo: Apex 처리 기간 5영업일이 현재의 절반 수준(roughly half the current turnaround)이라고 했으므로, 현재는 약 10영업일이 걸린다고 추론할 수 있습니다.

questions.q: The word "retired" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
choices: discontinued
resigned
withdrawn
relocated
questions.exKo: 여기서 retired는 시스템이 '단계적으로 폐지된다'는 뜻이므로 discontinued가 가장 가깝습니다. resign은 사람이 사임할 때 씁니다.
